title: DTLS role inverted for non-actpass setup attributes in WHIP ingest
test: tests/whip.test.js: "WHIP remote DTLS role is '<role>' for a <media|session>-level a=setup:<value> offer" (active and passive failed before the fix; actpass and absent passed before and after); "WHIP answer says a=setup:<value> in every section for a <level>-level a=setup:<value> offer, matching remote role '<role>'" (active and passive failed before the fix); "WHIP answer takes one a=setup from the section that supplies the DTLS parameters, for every section" (failed before); "WHIP answer for a setup:actpass offer is unchanged apart from the o= line" (golden captured from the unchanged serializer; passed before and after)
proof: Before the fix, node --test tests/whip.test.js ran 36 tests with 9 failures. parseDtlsParameters returned role 'server' for a=setup:active at media and session level (expected 'client') and 'client' for a=setup:passive at both levels (expected 'server'); createAnswer said a=setup:passive for every offer, so a passive offer got a passive answer and a client-role connect(), the deadlock the issue describes. After the fix parseDtlsParameters and createAnswer take the role and the a=setup from one helper (dtlsRoles): passive offer -> remote role 'server' and a=setup:active in every answered section; active, actpass or absent -> remote role 'client' and a=setup:passive. The actpass (OBS) answer equals the pre-change output apart from the o= line. tests/whip.test.js 36/36; full npm test 767/767; lint and typecheck pass.
